parsed.why: State-directed targeting: police register of LGBTIQ people, entrapment via fake meetings, extortion, raids with forced HIV testing, sham marriages, police inaction. Repressive state, no protections, hostile society. Organised targeting dominates.

Decriminalised 2022 by court; no protections, no LGR, no documented post-repeal enforcement or trans-specific incidents. Thin data, no recorded hostility toward travellers; 2005 cruise exclusion was ad hoc. No relief, no exposure.

Working protections: gender-identity discrimination law with damages awarded, hate-crime law, detention standards placing by lived gender. Documented campaigns against trans inclusion and one state's youth-care pause are frictions, not traveller exposures.

Strong legal framework (self-ID, marriage, conversion-therapy ban) and pride with police protection, but custody placement by birth sex with documented deaths, sexual violence and impunity in male prisons — a foreign trans woman was detained in a male pavilion. Rising violence amid conflict.

Protections on paper, hate-crime training and detainee name guidelines, but police disregard complaints, attackers unpunished, documented nationalist kidnappings of trans women, no case since 2014. Hostile heteronormative society, weak enforcement; thin current record.
